scenario: IELTS JSON SCHEMA INTEGRATION INSTRUCTIONS & DO'S AND DON'TS
description: Comprehensive specification guidelines, Good formats vs Bad formats, schema design rules, validation constraints, and layout parameters for full rendering compatibility.

dos: DO use the correct 'type' string identifiers matching the system components: 'MCQ' (Single Selection), 'MULTI_MCQ' (Multiple Selection), 'TF' (True/False/Not Given), 'YN' (Yes/No/Not Given), 'BLANK' (Fill in the Blank), 'INLINE_BLANKS' (Paragraph with Inline Blanks), 'MATCHING' (Matching Headings/Information), 'reading-passage', 'audio', 'image', 'video', 'divider', 'tip', 'band-descriptor', 'step', 'part1', 'cue-card', 'part3', 'task1', 'task2'.

DO design multi-question sets or complex Reading tests with 'layout_type': 'split', putting content resources (e.g. 'reading-passage', 'audio', 'image') under 'blocks.left' and the active interactive questions (e.g. 'MCQ', 'INLINE_BLANKS', 'MATCHING') under 'blocks.right' to generate responsive side-by-side splits.
DO use a single 'question-range' block to provide the heading (range) and instructions for a group of questions. This prevents duplication of instruction text within individual question blocks.

DO format 'INLINE_BLANKS' questions with distinct input placeholders using either '_____' (five underscores) or '[BLANK]' as markers inside the 'text' string (or array of strings joined with newlines). Make sure to supply the corresponding answers as a single string divided by vertical pipes '|' (e.g., 'water|sand|oxygen') under the 'correctAnswer' key. The system will map each placeholder to a distinct sub-question.

DO format 'MATCHING' blocks using two sets of parallel options: write prompts inside the 'text' block separated by newlines ('
') and write the correct matched answers in the same order inside the 'correctAnswer' string, also separated by newlines ('
') (e.g., 'A
C
B'). This maps each line into a standalone interactive drop-down matchup row.

DO specify correct answers for single selection 'MCQ' blocks using either 'correctIndex' (the integer index, e.g. 0, 1, 2) or 'correctAnswer' matching the exact character label (e.g. 'A', 'B', 'C', 'D').
DO provide multiple correct index answers under 'correctIndexes' (an array of integers, e.g. [0, 2]) for 'MULTI_MCQ' blocks to support multi-select validation.
DO ensure distinct IDs are generated as unique alphanumeric strings for every block to avoid DOM collisions, component re-mounting issues, or mixed state caching in localStorage.
DO use uppercase values ('TRUE', 'FALSE', 'NOT GIVEN' or 'YES', 'NO', 'NOT GIVEN') for 'TF' and 'YN' question validation to prevent validation mismatch bypass.

DO analyze Markdown input to determine how many questions belong to each section (e.g. Passage 1 / Section 1 = Q1–13, Passage 2 / Section 2 = Q14–27, Passage 3 / Section 3 = Q28–40), and explicitly attach 'sectionNumber': 1, 2, or 3 (and 'data.sectionNumber': 1|2|3) to EVERY passage block in 'blocks.left' and EVERY question/instruction block in 'blocks.right'. This gives the Course Designer a clear view of which questions belong to which section.

DO insert 'divider' blocks ({ "type": "divider" }) in 'blocks.left' between reading passages and in 'blocks.right' between question sets for different sections. The Course Designer uses the 'divider' block as an explicit section boundary: encountering a divider in 'blocks.left' or 'blocks.right' splits content from that point onwards into the next section (Section 1 -> Section 2 -> Section 3).

DO ensure each question block specifies its exact question range or question number (e.g. questionNumber: 1, startQNum: 14) along with 'sectionNumber': 1|2|3 so that questions can be cleanly filtered and grouped by section without any section bleeding.
donts: DONT duplicate instructions or headings inside individual question blocks (data.instruction, data.sectionHeading) if a 'question-range' block is already providing them for that set.

DONT mix questions of different sections together or allow Section 3 questions to bleed into Section 2 or Section 1. Ensure every question block's section metadata ('sectionNumber': 1|2|3) or question range strictly belongs to its respective reading section.
DONT omit 'sectionNumber' / 'section' metadata from question blocks or passage blocks when generating multi-section reading tests from Markdown or text input.
DONT provide plain unstructured question text without appropriate placeholders in 'INLINE_BLANKS' blocks. If no '_____' or '[BLANK]' is detected in the text, sub-question mapping will fail.

DONT mix different representations of MCQ index validations — if correct choice is index 0, do not declare it as string '0' in 'correctAnswer' without matching keys, and avoid inconsistency in labeling indices vs character options.

DONT wrap raw objects inside 'text' properties in your questions; always ensure the text is either a plain string or an array of strings that can be formatted. Objects will render as '[object Object]' layouts on the frontend.
DONT exceed a standard array length match inside matching paragraphs and keys — if there are 3 matching rows, there must be exactly 3 answer groups separated by newlines.
DONT expose sensitive credentials or database connection elements inside any instructions or schema fields.

DONT leave layout lists empty if children exist — e.g. if 'layout_type' is 'single', populate 'blocks.single' and leave 'left' and 'right' empty, while if 'layout_type' is 'split', leave 'single' empty and populate 'left' and 'right'.

MCQ.error_pattern: Declaring correct choices as alphabetical string labels like 'A' when the validation component only expects integer indices via 'correctIndex', causing a script crash during comparison.

INLINE_BLANKS.error_pattern: Failing to match the count of underline/blank placeholders to correct answers split by vertical pipes, causing out-of-bounds evaluation or unvalidated blank inputs.

data.text: First blank: _____ and second blank: _____

MATCHING.error_pattern: Formatting prompt or correct answer items inside raw arrays rather than newline-joined strings, which forces standard components to fail at line-splitting or render literal JSON fragments.

troubleshooting.unanswered_validation_glitches: Ensure every question block contains a populated 'id' key. Component modules map state to 'answers[q.id]' - if multiple questions share the same value or have no layout id, writing one input field triggers multiple component re-renders or overrides unrelated fields.
troubleshooting.whitespace_normalization: The compiler checks student responses by running '.trim().toLowerCase()'. However, avoid extra white space inside correctAnswer strings representing keys (e.g. use 'lead' instead of ' lead '), as exact options or splits should be clean.
troubleshooting.case_sensitivity_notes: All text completions and blanks are compared via case-insensitive matching, but the correct configuration keys should ideally match clean dictionary forms to support precise explanations.

data.title: Passage 1: Light Below the Sunlit Zone
data.text: Deep sea bioluminescence functions primarily as a defensive mechanism. In the twilight zones (200m - 1000m), marine creatures synthesize luciferin compounds to signal mates or startle micro-predators. Unlike surface species that rely on ambient light waves, deep-sea organisms utilize highly concentrated chemical interactions that emit short-wavelength blue light, which travels furthest underwater.
